sentences.text: Criminal Revision Case No.1283 Of 2013
Order :

The revision petitioner was convicted for the offence punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and sentenced to one year Rigorous Imprisonment by the trial Court.
The said conviction was confirmed in appeal by the Sessions Court.
2. Briefly, the case against the revision petitioner is that he was Proprietor of a shop selling oils such as Cotton Seed oil, Soyabeen oil, Groundnut oil etc.
The Food Inspector-PW.1 along with independent persons went to the shop and purchased 375 grams of Cotton Seed Oil and divided it into three samples.
On 28.01.2003, the Food Inspector dispatched one sample to the public analyst for opinion.
On 10.03.2003, the Food Inspector received public analyst report stating that the sample does not conform to the standards and it was adulterated.
PW.1 having received the public analyst report sought permission for launching prosecution.
Consent for launching prosecution was received on 04.10.2003.
Thereafter, PW.3-the other food inspector received the entire case record from PW.1-Food Inspector on 10.10.2003.
On 07.01.2004 he filed complaint along with the permission to prosecute the accused.
The Court took cognizance on 12.02.2004 and notices under Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act were sent vide registered post which was marked as Exs.P18 to P20.
The accused did not make request for samples to be analysed by the Central Lab.
3. The learned Magistrate examined PWs.1 to 3.
PWs.1 and 3 are the two inspectors.
PW.2 is the panch witness.
Exs. P1 to P20 were marked on behalf of the prosecution.
Ex . P11
is the analysis report.
Ex . P18
is the notice issued under Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
No material objects were marked by the prosecution.

4. Learned Magistrate found that PW.1 had carried out sampling in accordance with the procedure and the analysis report-Ex.P11 reflects that the oil was adulterated, since it did not conform to standards of Belier Test (Turbidity temperature acetic acid method) and saponification value.
Accordingly convicted the accused.
5. The said conviction was confirmed by the appellate Court in appeal.
6. Learned Counsel appearing for the revision petitioner would submit that there is violation under Section 11(4) and 13(2) of the Act.

Though there was no delay in sending notice under Section 13(2)
of the Act after complaint being filed, however, the said notice was not received by the accused.
The analysis report is dated 10.03.2003 whereas the notice under Section 13(2) of the Act was sent on 14.02.2004, which is nearly after one year.

sentences.text: On the other hand learned Assistant Public Prosecutor would submit that all the procedure prescribed under the Act has been followed and there is no violation of any procedure under Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.

8. Section 11(4) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act reads as follows;
"11.Procedure to be followed by food inspectors:
(4) An article of food seized under sub-section (4) of Section 10, unless destroyed under sub-section(4A) of that section, and any adulterant seized under sub- section (6) of that section shall be produced before a magistrate as soon as possible and in any case not later than seven days after the receipt of the report of the public analyst."
9. As seen from Section 11(4) of the Act an article of food unless destroyed, shall be produced before the Magistrate as soon as possible and in any case not later than seven days after receipt of the test report from public analyst.
10.

The argument of the learned counsel is that the seized sample should have been produced before the concerned Magistrate not later than 7 days after receipt of the report of the public analyst,
cannot be accepted.
Section 11(1)(2) deal with samples and 11(4) deals with the seized food article.
Even according to PW.1, only 3 samples were drawn and one sample was sent to the public analyst and two samples were sent to the local health authority for safe custody under Ex.P10.
Oil entirely was not seized as such the question of attracting section 11(4) of the Act does not arise.
The samples were dispatched in accordance with Section 11(1)(2) of the Act.

Section 11(4) deals with any sample food article that may be seized and has no application to the samples collected.
11.
The other argument of the learned counsel is that there was violation of Section 13(2) of the Act.
In fact, notices were sent on 14.02.2004 and received under Ex.P20.
I do not find that there is any violation of neither Section 11(4) or 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.

12. Keeping the nature of the offence which hs taken place nearly 21 years ago and there being no other criminal cases of similar kind against the petitioner, the sentence of imprisonment is reduced to the period already undergone by the revision petitioner.
However, the fine component is increased to Rs.15,000/-.

The said fine amount shall be paid within six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order, failing which the revision petitioner shall undergo default sentence of three months imprisonment.
13. Accordingly, Criminal Revision Case is partly allowed.
__ K.SURENDER, J Date: 24.09.2024 tk Vishwanadam Srinivas, Karimnagar Dt., vs State Of Ap., Rep. Pp., Hyd., on 24 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32871330/
